subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Read and understand the terms and conditions of an online club
Find the complaints in a formal e-mail
Write a formal e-mail of complaint

tf.s: You must be 18 or over to buy DVDs from the Online DVD Club.
tf.why: Yes! So a 19-year-old can buy DVDs.

tf.s: You can return any DVD after you have watched it.
tf.why: You can only return DVDs that are faulty.

tf.s: If you pay after three months, 10 percent is added.
tf.why: Right! You must pay within three months.

tf.s: You have to buy the recommended DVDs.
tf.why: You do not have to buy the recommended DVDs.

tf.s: Members must buy a minimum of ten DVDs a year for the first two years.
The complaint e-mail begins with 'Dear Sir or Madam'.
tf.why: Yes! This is a formal greeting.

tf.s: A formal complaint e-mail ends with 'Take care, speak soon'.
'I am writing to inform you…' is a formal phrase.
tf.why: Good! It is used to explain why you are writing.

tf.s: The customer wants to return the DVDs and not pay the extra 10 percent.

mcq.q: Why should you read the terms and conditions before you join an online club?
o: To know the rules before you agree to them
mcq.why: Terms tell you what you must and must not do.

mcq.q: Which is the best first sentence of a complaint about a wrong book?
o: I am writing to inform you that I received the wrong book.
